text: But look closely at how Cornell built it, because the sorting was there from the very start.
This was never meant to be a place for everyone, and he never pretended otherwise.
He marketed Hyde Park as selective by design.
He sold large lots, the kind only the well-off could afford, and he leaned hard on the lake in every advertisement, fine lake views, room to breathe, the right sort of neighbors.
The closer you stood to the water, the more the ground was worth.
He kept heavy industry out of the heart of his development so the smoke and the noise and the men who worked in them would stay somewhere else.
The factories and the cheaper workers' cottages went to other parts of the sprawling township, away from the shoreline, while the lakefront stayed expensive and quiet.
From the very beginning, then, the map had a grain to it.
Wealth gathered by the lake in the north, and everything cheaper was pushed outward and southward.
Cornell did not stumble into that pattern.
